comparisons.basis: A short rounded sign followed by a looping/crossing stroke appears alike at the candidate locations. However, I cannot confidently establish both complete supplied group boundaries against their following bench-like strokes from this view. Similarity of that short motif alone does not settle identity of the complete ordered groups.

Both visible short motifs have a descending left stroke with a small head/cross-stroke, followed by a rounded body and then a looping/crossing terminal stroke, in that order. Their proportions and pen angles differ, but I do not see an added or omitted major motif within the compared short groups.

The compared low horizontal/bench-like beginnings continue through a similar series of small curved strokes into an upright looped feature and a descending terminal tail. The whole visible progression resembles a repeat despite differences in spread and curvature. Exact counts or atomic identities of the small strokes are not established.

The later .44 short motif again has the descending left element, rounded body and looping/crossing terminal element in the same apparent order as the far-right .43 motif. The following taller cluster appears spatially separate; exact transcription-level segmentation is not independently established here.

The two neighboring longer groups repeat the same apparent progression: descending initial element, small rounded body, conspicuous tall paired/looping strokes, low curved continuation, another looped feature and terminal descending tail. Differences in width, slant and ink do not show a clear change to that ordered motif sequence.
